### Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) & Constructive Alignment

This session turns from concepts to course design. It introduces Education for Sustainable Development as a
distinct pedagogical approach, and constructive alignment as the design tool that translates ESD principles into a
concrete, well-aligned course unit or course.

:::

---

## Session Overview

| | |
|---|---|
| **Duration** | Approx. 95-105 min self-paced (equivalent to a 2h live session) |
| **Preparation for participants** | Completion of Session 2, including the "identify opportunities" task |

---

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this session, participants will be able to:

1. Gain an understanding of the principles and importance of Education for Sustainable Development (ESD).
2. Gain an understanding of the concept of constructive alignment in designing effective courses.

---

## Session Outline

::: {.session-topics}

**1. Opening plenary discussion** (10 min)
: Recap of the Session 2 task, opportunities identified and disciplinary links to SD.

**2. Introduction to ESD** (25 min)

**3. Discussion/reflection** (10 min)
: Teaching principles participants already apply.

**4. Introduction to Constructive Alignment** (25 min)

**5. Examples of Constructive Alignment** (15 min)
: Land degradation, urban migration.

**6. Reflection** ("muddiest point")

**7. Task after Session 3** (session development) and outlook on Session 4.

:::

## Preparation tasks & learning activities

::: {.callout-note .callout-before appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Before the session**

Have the Session 2 task (opportunities to incorporate SD into your course) at hand; it is revisited at the start of
this session.
:::

::: {.callout-tip .callout-during appearance="simple" icon=false}
**During the session**

- Complete the reflection on teaching principles you currently apply.
- Work through the two worked examples of constructive alignment (land degradation, urban migration).
- Complete the "muddiest point" reflection.
:::

::: {.callout-warning .callout-after appearance="simple" icon=false}
**After the session**

Task after Session 3, session development: find a topic related to SD in your own discipline and develop a
lesson/session using constructive alignment, at least three learning outcomes, suitable learning activities, and a
matching assessment format. Prepare a short (approx. 6-minute) presentation of your action plan for Session 4.
:::

## Recommendation for facilitation

- Use a shared digital board (e.g. Padlet) or an equivalent tool for the "muddiest point" task, so responses can be
  reviewed and addressed collectively. As facilitator, review all "muddiest points" before the next session and
  prepare answers for the questions raised.
- After presenting the land degradation and urban migration examples, ask participants to sketch how the same
  three-element alignment could look for a topic in their own discipline, this is where transfer actually happens.
- The "teaching principles" reflection works well as a cross-disciplinary sharing moment: participants from
  different fields often name different principles.
